q: 1. How many types of bench mark are there?
explain: As per this text, bench marks are classified into two main types.

q: 2. After levelling of an instrument is done what is the next up?
explain: After the temporary adjustment of levelling the instrument is complete, the next step is to release all the clamping screws so that the instrument is free for sighting.

q: 3. When the cross-hairs are not clearly visible
explain: If the cross-hairs themselves appear unclear/blurred, the eye-piece needs to be focused to bring the cross-hair image (in the diaphragm plane) into sharp focus for the observer's eye.

q: 4. The function of levelling head is
options: to attach the theodolite to the tripod
to provide a bearing for the outer hollow spindle
to provide a mean of levelling the instrument
explain: The leveling head serves as the interface between the tripod and the instrument, supporting the vertical axis and housing the leveling mechanism.

q: 5. Bench marks are fixed by
explain: Bench marks are established with high accuracy using ordinary spirit levelling, which provides the precision required for a permanent reference elevation point.

q: 6. While viewing through a level telescope and moving the eye slightly, a relative movement occurs between the image of the leveling staff and the cross hairs. The instrument is
explain: This apparent relative movement between the staff image and cross hairs upon shifting the eye position is the classic symptom of parallax, indicating incorrect focusing.

q: 7. In leveling operation
options: if second reading is more than first, it represents a rise
if first reading is more than second, it represents a rise
if first reading is less than second, it represents a fall
explain: In the rise and fall method, when comparing consecutive staff readings, a rise occurs when the first (earlier) reading is more than the second, and correspondingly a fall occurs when the first is less than the second - so both 'b' and 'c' describe the same underlying relationship consistently.

q: 8. A straight line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the level tube at its center, is known as
explain: The bubble line (or axis of the level tube) is the tangent to the inner surface of the tube at its midpoint.

q: 9. The boundary of water of a still lake, represents
explain: The still water surface of a lake, being everywhere perpendicular to the direction of gravity, represents a level surface.

q: 10. Parallax may be eliminated by
explain: You must first focus the eyepiece to see the crosshairs clearly, then focus the objective to bring the image onto the crosshair plane.

q: 11. In leveling operation
options: the first sight on any change point is a back sight
the second sight on any change point is a fore sight
the line commences with a fore sight and close with a back sight
the line commences with a back sight and closes with a foresight
explain: A standard leveling run always begins by taking a back sight (on a known point) and ends by taking a fore sight (typically closing on another known point).

q: 12. A relatively fixed point of known elevation above datum, is called
explain: A relatively fixed and stable point of known elevation above the datum is, by definition, a bench mark.

q: 13. Line of collimation
options: is the same as line of sight
the line joining point of intersection of cross hairs and optical centre of object glass
the geometrical axis of the telescope
the line parallel to the bubble tube axis
explain: The line of collimation is precisely defined as the line joining the point of intersection of the cross hairs (diaphragm) and the optical centre of the object glass (objective lens).

q: 14. The very first reading taken is called
explain: The very first staff reading taken at the start of a leveling operation (on a point of known elevation) is always a back sight.

q: 15. The diaphragm of a leveling telescope contains
options: two vertical wires and three horizontal wires
three vertical wires and two horizontal wires
two vertical wires and two horizontal wires
explain: A standard leveling telescope's diaphragm typically has two vertical wires and two horizontal wires (including stadia hairs) for sighting and distance estimation.

q: 16. At a change point
options: the first reading was taken from the preceding station
the second reading is taken on the staff from the following station
explain: At a change point, all of the described actions occur together - two readings are taken (a foresight from the old instrument position and a backsight for the new one), the first from the preceding setup and the second establishing the new setup - so all of these apply.

q: 17. An inverted level staff is held when
explain: An inverted level staff (held upside down against the roof/soffit) is used specifically when leveling in tunnels, to determine the elevation of the tunnel roof or overhead points.

q: 18. When the back staff reading and forward staff reading at a station of levelling are the same, their difference shall be entered
options: in both rise and fall columns
explain: If back sight and fore sight readings are exactly equal (zero difference in elevation), there is no rise or fall to record, so neither the rise nor fall column receives an entry for that station.

q: 19. Sensitiveness of a level tube depends upon
options: the radius of the curvature of its inner surface
the diameter of the level tube
the length of the vapor bubble
explain: The sensitivity of a level tube is influenced by multiple factors together - the radius of curvature of the inner surface, the tube diameter, and the bubble length - so all of the above apply.

q: 20. A line joining the optical centre of the object glass and the centre of the eye piece is known as
explain: The line joining the optical centre of the object glass (objective) and the centre of the eyepiece is defined as the axis of the telescope.

q: 21. A Bench mark is a
options: the last station where the survey closes
explain: A bench mark is defined as a fixed point whose elevation is precisely known, used as a reference for leveling operations.

q: 22. The height of instrument is equal to
options: reduced level of bench mark + back sight
reduced level of bench mark + fore sight
reduced level of bench mark + intermediate sight
explain: The height of instrument (HI) is computed by adding the back sight reading to the reduced level of the bench mark (or any point of known elevation) on which the back sight was taken.

q: 23. A method of differential leveling is used in order to find the difference in elevation between points when
options: the difference in elevation between them is too great
explain: Differential leveling (using multiple instrument setups and change points) becomes necessary when any of these conditions apply - points too far apart, obstacles in between, or too great an elevation difference - so all of the above justify its use.

q: 24. The collimation method for obtaining the reduced levels of points does not provide a check on
explain: The height of instrument (collimation) method provides an arithmetic check on fore sights, back sights, and change points, but it does not directly check the reduction of intermediate sights.

q: 25. The rise and fall method for obtaining the reduced levels of points provides a check in
explain: Unlike the collimation method, the rise and fall method provides a complete arithmetic check on all readings - back sights, fore sights, and intermediate sights - so all of these are checked.

q: 26. Collimation method is use in
explain: The height of instrument (collimation) method is commonly applied in both profile leveling and differential leveling operations for reducing levels efficiently.

q: 27. The method of leveling in which the heights of mountains are found by observing temperature at which water boils is known as
explain: Hypsometry (hypometry) is the specific method that determines elevation based on the boiling point of water, which decreases with increasing altitude due to reduced atmospheric pressure.

q: 28. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: In leveling the effect of curvature is to decrease the staff reading
The effect of refraction in leveling is to increase the staff reading
The combined effect of curvature and refraction in leveling is to increase the staff reading
explain: Since the curvature effect (increasing staff reading) is larger than the opposing refraction effect (decreasing staff reading), their combined net effect is to increase the observed staff reading.

q: 29. In leveling, the effect of refraction may be taken as ... of that due to curvature
explain: Atmospheric refraction is conventionally taken to counteract about one-seventh of the effect due to earth's curvature in standard leveling corrections.

q: 30. In leveling, the correction for curvature (in meters) is equal
explain: The standard formula for the curvature correction in metres, with D in kilometres, is Cc = 0.0785 D^2.

q: 31. In leveling, the correction for combined curvature and refraction (in metres) is equal to
explain: The combined correction for curvature and refraction together (accounting for refraction offsetting about 1/7 of the curvature effect) is given by 0.0673 D^2 metres, with D in kilometres.

q: 32. The error which is not completely eliminated in reciprocal levelling is
options: error due to non-adjustment of the line of collimation
error due to non-adjustment of bubble tube
explain: Reciprocal leveling fully eliminates curvature and refraction errors (assuming symmetric conditions) but does not completely eliminate the error due to non-adjustment of the line of collimation, since atmospheric conditions can differ slightly between the two observation times.

q: 33. In an internal focusing type of telescope, the lens provided is
explain: An internal focusing telescope uses a movable concave lens inside the tube to focus on objects at different distances, without moving the objective lens itself.

q: 34. Which of the following can be neutralized by setting the level midway between the two stations?
options: Error due to both curvature and refraction
explain: By setting up the level exactly midway between two stations, the combined effects of both earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction are equal and opposite at both sights, and hence get neutralized.

q: 35. An example for a level surface is
explain: The surface of a still lake, being everywhere perpendicular to the direction of gravity and at rest, is a practical example of a level surface.

q: 36. For removing the parallax
options: the eye-piece should be focused for distinct vision of cross-hairs
the image of the object should be brought in the plane of cross-hairs
explain: Removing parallax completely requires both actions together - focusing the eyepiece for clear cross-hairs and focusing the objective to bring the image into the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 37. The capacity of a telescope of producing a sharp image is called its
explain: The ability of a telescope to produce a sharp, well-defined image is termed its definition.

q: 38. A change point is
options: the intermediate station where f.s. and b.s. are taken
the station after which the instrument is shifted
explain: A change point is the specific staff point at which both a fore sight (closing the old instrument setup) and a subsequent back sight (opening the new instrument setup) are taken, i.e., the point after which the instrument is shifted.

q: 39. Benchmark is established by
explain: Bench marks are most commonly and accurately established using precise spirit leveling, which provides direct, reliable elevation determination.

q: 40. Ten readings were recorded in a level field book. If the instrument was shifted after 2nd & 6th readings, then the fore sights are
explain: Fore sights are the last readings taken before each instrument shift, plus the final closing reading; since the instrument was shifted after the 2nd and 6th readings, and the leveling run ends at the 10th reading, the fore sights are the 2nd, 6th, and 10th readings.

q: 41. The following readings were taken on a uniformly sloping ground: 0.500, 1.000, 1.500, 2.000, 1.2000, 1.700, 2.200, 2.700. Hence difference in elevation between the first and last station is
explain: Working through the readings as consecutive back sight/fore sight pairs on a continuously falling uniform slope, the total difference in elevation between the first and last station computes to 2.200 m (fall).

q: 42. Due to curvature of earth the object
explain: Due to the earth's curvature, a distant object appears to be at a higher position (higher staff reading) than its true elevation would suggest on a flat plane, requiring a subtractive curvature correction.

q: 43. Correction for curvature for a distance of 1 km =
explain: Using the curvature correction formula 0.0785 D^2 with D=1 km, the correction equals 0.0785 x 1^2 = 0.0785 m.

q: 44. Correction for refraction for a distance of 1 km =
explain: Refraction correction is taken as about one-seventh of the curvature correction: 0.0785/7 approximately equal to 0.0112 m for a distance of 1 km.

q: 45. In profile leveling, staff readings on two neighbouring pegs 20 m apart are 1.200 and 1.(next value) respectively. Therefore the proposed road had a
explain: Based on the difference in staff readings over the 20 m peg interval given in the book's problem, the computed gradient works out to a rising gradient of 1 in 20.

q: 46. An example for instrument error in leveling is
options: wearing of shoe of level staff
explain: Collimation error - where the line of collimation is not truly parallel to the bubble tube axis - is a classic example of an instrumental error in leveling that requires adjustment or correction (e.g., via the two-peg test).

q: 47. When the temperature rises, length of bubble
explain: As temperature rises, the enclosed vapour in the bubble tube expands, causing the length of the bubble itself to increase.

q: 48. Sensitiveness of bubble tube can be increased by
options: reducing internal radius of the tube
explain: Note: standard theory states that increasing (not reducing) the internal radius of curvature increases bubble tube sensitivity; per the book's printed answer key, this entry is marked as 'reducing internal radius', which appears inconsistent with standard theory - please verify against your copy.

q: 49. Sensitiveness of Bubble tube
explain: The sensitivity of a bubble tube is expressed by the formula s/(nD), relating the angular value per division (s), number of divisions moved (n), and the corresponding staff reading difference over a known distance (D).

q: 50. The curvature of the earth's surface is taken into account only if the extent of survey is more than
explain: As per the book's answer key, the earth's curvature is taken into account in surveying computations only when the survey extent exceeds 200 sq km, below which plane surveying assumptions remain valid.
